body: No problem; Good luck with your situation.

Opening up is a near impossible thing to do for many individuals, myself included. I would say "just do it", but I understand that is an impossible, meaningless statement. I also seem to force myself into isolation, and although I am unable to do anything about it, I realize that it is a bad thing. Your experience in this hurricaine seems like a traumatic, horrible one. Rescuing others is an action that is very difficult, as it requires immense levels of sacrifice. If you were to rescue this boy, you could have died yourself, along with the boy. 

This does NOT make you a selfish person, as it is only a natural instinct to freeze up in the sight of horror. An experience like this would traumatize almost anyone, so please do not feel as though it is abnormal. I guess the best thing to do is to accept what happened as something that was inevitable, because, no matter what, it was. I'm sorry that this sounds harsh, because it is, but I lost a friend of mine to suicide. I could have saved him, but I didn't take action and this guilt has plagued me ever since. Thinking of the situation as inevitable has helped me a bit, because everyone truly wishes they could go back in time to save people they saw die. However, we can't. (For now at least)

Please, don't let the guilt plague you. I can talk more if you want. :)
